headline: Where Is the Model Number on a Washer, Dryer, Fridge and Dishwasher?
sub: It is almost never on the front.

Dishwasher: On the tub frame or edge, visible with the door open

headline: Model Number vs Serial Number: What Each One Is For
sub: Both are usually on the same plate, so photograph the whole plate and write both down.
items: Model number: identifies the product design and is what you use to order parts
Serial number: identifies your specific unit and is what warranty and recall checks use
proof: The model number identifies the product design and is what you use to order parts. The serial number identifies your specific unit and is what warranty and recall checks use. Both are usually on the same plate, so photograph the whole plate and write both down.

headline: How to Save an Appliance Model Number So You Can Find It Again

Photograph the whole plate, then a close shot of each code
Type the model and serial into whatever you keep records in
Note the year you bought it and where

headline: What If the Appliance Model Number Sticker Is Worn Off? Where to Look Next
sub: These usually work, in roughly this order.
items: The original receipt or order confirmation email
The manual or the box, if either survived
A past repair invoice
The retailer's account or the maker's registration, if you registered the product
proof: Worn, painted over, hidden behind cabinetry or peeled off. These usually work, in roughly this order.
The original receipt or order confirmation email. Search your inbox for the brand.
The manual or the box, if either survived.
A past repair invoice. Technicians almost always write the model on it.
The retailer's account or the maker's registration, if you registered the product.

headline: Appliance Info to Record: The Extra Line for Fridge, Furnace and Water Heater
sub: The five fields cover most things. A few categories are worth one extra line.
items: Refrigerator: Water filter part number, and the replacement interval printed inside
Furnace or central air: Filter size, and whether it's a standard 1 inch or a thicker media filter
Water heater: Tank size in gallons, and the fuel type: gas or electric
Garage door opener: Remote or keypad type, not the code itself
